{{short description|Chinese and British applied mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=September 2020}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=September 2020}}
'''Xiaoyu Luo''' ({{lang-zh|罗小玉}},{{r|xjtu}} 1960{{r|nwpu}} – 5 February 2025{{r|funeral}}) was a Chinese and British applied mathematician who studied [[biomechanics]], [[fluid dynamics]], and the interactions of fluid flows with soft biological tissues. She was a professor of applied mathematics at the [[University of Glasgow]].{{r|frse}}
==Education and career==
Luo was born in the UK{{r|nwpu}} but grew up in [[Xi'an]] in a family of artists.{{r|cv}} After earning bachelor's and master's degrees in theoretical mechanics at [[Xi'an Jiaotong University]], in 1982 and 1985 respectively, she became a lecturer at Xi'an Jiaotong University. There, she studied for a Ph.D. from 1987 until 1990,{{r|cv|orcid}} with a visit to the UK through a joint doctoral program with the [[University of Sheffield]]. When she earned her Ph.D. at Xi'an Jiaotong University in 1990, she became the first woman to do so.{{r|cv}}
She moved to the UK in 1992 to become a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Leeds]]. She worked as a lecturer in engineering at [[Queen Mary and Westfield College]] from 1997 to 2000, and in mechanical engineering at the [[University of Sheffield]] from 2000 to 2004, before becoming a senior lecturer in mathematics at the University of Glasgow in 2005. She was promoted to professor in 2008,{{r|cv|orcid}} the first female professor of applied mathematics at Glasgow.{{r|nwpu}}
In 2014 she was named a chair professor at [[Northwestern Polytechnical University]] in Xi'an.{{r|nwpu}} She has also been a visitor to the International Center for Applied Mechanics at Xi'an Jiaotong University.{{r|xjtu}}
==Death==
Luo died on 5 February 2025 at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital in Glasgow, aged 64.{{r|funeral}}
==Recognition==
Luo became a [[Fellow of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers]] in 2004{{r|cv}} and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2014.{{r|frse|cv}}
